cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Rebuild the week around what your body can actually recover from — three loaded days, not five.
Groove a trunk-supported hinge so your lower back earns the barbell back next cycle.
Build your first ever cardio base and a daily ten-minute back routine.

paragraphs: You've been training five days a week and going hard, and nothing has moved. That's not because you haven't tried. Your body has been getting a lot of stress and not much room to recover, so it's been holding on instead of changing.

So this month we do something that will feel strange. Three real gym days instead of five, a little lighter than you're used to, and we add walking. This block is about building the floor. We're not chasing the scale yet.

By the end of four weeks I want three things from you: you turned up, your back felt good on every hinge, and your walk got longer each week. Get those and the next block can do the fat loss properly.
outcomes: Every hinge session finished pain free
A real working weight found and logged on every exercise
Four weeks of the daily back routine done

cycles.name: Slow Burn
focuses: Your first real fat-loss phase, on a routine that finally holds.
A fourth day comes back, and the free hinge returns as a skill.

paragraphs: Cycle 2 is where the fat loss actually starts. A fourth day comes back, your food gets its first real change, and the walking turns into proper work.
But it only opens if your back stays quiet this month. That's the deal, and it's the whole reason we go slow now.
Keep the back quiet and the next one is yours.

cycles.name: Metabolic Override
focuses: Push the fat loss properly — this is where the mirror starts to change.
First interval work, on a base you spent nine weeks building.

cycles.name: Strength Reclaim
focuses: A planned break from the deficit, spent getting genuinely strong.
The barbell hinge comes back, earned by three clean cycles.

cycles.name: Final Cut
focuses: The last push, on the freshest recovery you'll have had all programme.
Then a planned landing, so what you built actually stays.

cards.title: Why Three Days, Not Five
cards.body:
You already train five days. Dropping to three loaded days is going to feel like going backwards. It isn't. Five hard days with no recovery is exactly why nothing changed.

You've had a heavy month, and your body knows it even when your head is busy. Less load right now means your training finally gets used instead of just survived.

You still keep your five days if you want them. Day 2 and Day 4 are walk and stretch days and they count as showing up. Turning up is the win this month, not how hard you went.

cards.title: How To Pick Your Weight
cards.body:
I never put a number on your card. You find it every session against the RPE target. RPE 7 means you finish the set with about 3 good reps left in you.

  • New exercise: go light on the first set. If it felt like a 6, add weight next set. If it was a real grind, take some off. That first set is information, not a wasted set.
  • Next week, same exercise: hit all your reps at or under the target RPE, go up a small step. Missed reps or it felt way too hard, stay at the same weight and do it again.
  • Bad day: drop the weight. That is the system working, not you failing.

Week 1 is calibration. Keep everything at a 6 and just learn the machines. The RPE 7 target opens from week 2.

cards.title: Your Back, And When To Stop
cards.body:
You've had lower back trouble before, so this cycle takes the free deadlift and the squat off the table and gives you supported work instead. The 45° back extension on Day 3 is doing the same job with your hips held. A quiet month here is what earns the barbell back next cycle.

Normal and fine: muscle burn, being tired, stiff either side of your spine the next day. Keep training through that.

  • Mild ache that fades: finish the set, write it in your log.
  • Ache that builds through the set, or changes how you move: stop that exercise, carry on with the rest of the session without it, and message me.
  • Sharp, one sided, or anything running down your leg: stop the session. Walk if you want. Message me before your next one.

Nothing on this list makes you a difficult client. I'd rather hear about it in week 1 than fix it in week 4.

cards.title: Your Period Week
cards.body:
You don't need to plan anything on those days. Come in and use this.

  • Keep all of it: your walks, Day 2 and Day 4, glute bridges, the stretching. Light movement usually helps the cramping.
  • Cut to 2 sets and go visibly lighter: hip thrust, leg press, the back extension, single leg press. Move the pattern, don't grind it.
  • Skip completely: dead bug, side plank, bird dog, plank. Hard bracing through your stomach on those days is not worth it.

A cut down day still counts as a session. Log it as normal so I can see the week properly.

cards.title: Protein Without The Calories
cards.body:
You told me your calories jump every time you push your protein up. That's a food choice problem, not a discipline problem. You're adding protein on top of your meals instead of swapping it in.

Same idea every time. Keep the meal, change the protein for a leaner version of itself.

  • Chicken thigh becomes chicken breast. Same plate, a lot fewer calories.
  • Full fat yoghurt or cheese becomes low fat or Greek yoghurt.
  • Nuts and peanut butter are fat first, protein second. Nice food, bad protein source.
  • Eggs are great, but 3 whole eggs plus 2 whites beats 5 whole eggs.

We're not cutting your food this month, so don't start counting anything yet. Just start swapping. We'll set real numbers together at the next check in once I can see how you actually eat.

cards.title: The Walk Is Training
cards.body:
You've never done cardio, and it's the one big thing missing. That's actually good news. It means we have a lever nobody has pulled yet.

Pace matters more than speed here. You should be able to talk in full sentences the whole way. If you're breathing too hard to finish a sentence, slow it down or drop the incline.

It gets 2 to 3 minutes longer each week, and that's it. Don't jump ahead and don't add extra sessions. Going too hard too early is how we rebuild the exact tiredness we're trying to get rid of.

cards.title: What We Actually Measure
cards.body:
Your medication changed your weight, and it can hide what's really happening on the scale for weeks. So the scale is the last thing I trust this month, not the first.

What I want instead: photos once a month in the same light, a tape measure round your waist and hips, how your clothes sit, and how long you can walk. Those tell the truth when the scale is being noisy.

And be honest with yourself about this cycle. Nothing dramatic happens in four weeks and it isn't supposed to. This month builds the thing that makes month 2 and month 3 work.

cards.title: About Your Upper Body
cards.body:
You said your upper body feels too big, so let me be straight with you. You can't choose where fat comes off. There's no exercise, no machine and no diet that takes it from one place only. Anyone who tells you different is selling something.

What actually works is two things at once. Fat comes off everywhere as your food and your walking do their job. And we build your legs and glutes while your upper body just holds what it has.

That's why you've got a lot of leg work and only a few sets of pressing. Not training your upper body doesn't shrink it, it just makes it soft. Trust the plan and give it three months.

cards.title: You Already Brought Something
cards.body:
Before we change anything, look at what you walked in with. An 80kg hip thrust for 10 reps at your bodyweight is genuinely strong. That's not a beginner number.

You also kept showing up five days a week through a month most people would have stopped completely. The consistency is already there. That's the hard part and you have it.

What was missing was never effort. It was recovery and cardio, and both of those we can fix.

cards.title: When A Day Feels Too Much
cards.body:
Some days this month will be harder than others, and that's expected. You don't cancel, you shrink. Every session has a short version.

  • Rough day: take every RPE down by one. Six is the floor, never go under it.
  • Really rough day: do the first main lift and the walk, then leave. That still counts as a session.
  • Short on time: first main lift for 2 sets, the core work, and a 10 minute walk.

You can also do the days in a different order to fit your week. Week 4 is a lighter week on purpose — same exercises and same sets, just take some weight off the bar and hold your walk where week 3 left it.
